AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Practice guidelines recommend palliative care for patients with advanced cancer, but gaps in access and quality of care persist.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To increase goals-of-care (GOC) communication for hospitalized patients with Stage IV cancer.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: An interdisciplinary team designed a quality improvement intervention to enhance oncology palliative care, including training in communication skills and triggers for palliative care consults.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING/SUBJECTS
AbstractText.content: All adult inpatients with Stage IV cancer and unplanned admission at an 804-bed hospital affiliated with a National Cancer Institute (NCI) Comprehensive Cancer Center.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: The primary quality measure was the percentage of patients with Stage IV cancer who had a GOC discussion during hospitalization; secondary measures included screening for pain, dyspnea, spiritual needs, and outcomes of intensive care, hospice, and 30-day readmission.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: In the 11-month study period, n = 330, Stage IV cancer patients were hospitalized. Comparing the first three months with the final three months, rates of GOC discussion increased from 29% to 48% (p = 0.013), and specialty palliative care consultation increased from 18% to 33%, (p = 0.026). Rates of symptom screening, intensive care unit transfer, hospice, and 30-day re-admission did not change overall. However, patients with specialty palliative care more frequently had pain screening (91% vs. 81%, p = 0.020), spiritual assessment (48% vs. 10%, p < 0.001), and hospice referral (39% vs. 9%, p < 0.001), and they were less likely to be re-admitted within 30 days (12% vs. 21%, p = 0.059).

AbstractText.Label: DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: Interdisciplinary quality improvement was effective to increase GOC discussions and palliative care consults for patients with Stage IV cancer.
